Subject: Dedicated capacity options for Silverpine - cluster sizing & ramp

Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the load tests over the weekend and wanted to share a short summary and ask for concrete proposal options for a dedicated reservation. High-level needs below: 

- Peak concurrency: ~420 requests/minute with bursts to 700 for short windows
- Daily token volume (inference only): ~1.1M - 1.4M tokens/day (user prompts + responses)
- Latency target: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 700ms for our primary 30B model; we will also run a smaller 7B for fan-out rerank tasks
- Stable traffic expected in 6–8 months, but we need a predictable near-term runway for product experiments

Questions we need covered in the proposal:
1) Minimum guaranteed GPUs for a production lane that meets the above latency targets (include model assumptions: 30B quantized fp16/4-bit runtimes)
2) Suggested cluster sizing options (starter, baseline, growth) with expected throughput per node and headroom for bursts
3) Recommended ramp (week-by-week or month-by-month) and warm-start windows for model prewarmed KV caches
4) Any recommended burst/standing-by architecture (hot-standby, preemption tolerances) and penalties/credits

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our observed QPS distribution and token histogram. Also copy our contracts address (contracts@silverpine.ai) on the thread — they'll need the SLA and term options.

Appreciate a written options set we can share with Finance and Engineering.

Best,
Evan
Evan Brooks
VP Product, Silverpine AI

Team / Evan — draft proposal below (high level). I'll produce a pricing summary and a one‑page DocuSign-ready term sheet after we pick which option Silverpine prefers.

Option A — Fast Start (Experimental + Prod canary)- Minimum reserved: 8 GPUs (A100 L40 equiv)- Topology: single rack of 8 GPUs; supports one 30B quantized instance with modest concurrency via batching- Expected steady throughput: ~200–300 reqs/minute (p50 ~180ms on 30B)- Use case: quick runway for product experiments and canary prod; lower monthly commit- Activation: 2–3 week lead time for dedicated pool + 1 week of prewarm (KV cache)- Burst strategy: limited burst via hosted spillover (best-effort)

Option B — Production Baseline (Recommended starting point)- Minimum reserved: 32 GPUs (4 x 8-GPU nodes)- Topology: 4 nodes with autoscale headroom in the dedicated pool for contiguous lanes- Expected steady throughput: 450–550 reqs/minute for the 30B quantized profile (p50 ~130–180ms) with p95 ~600ms- Use case: supports primary traffic with room for growth; enables rollouts and A/B tests- Activation: 4–6 week lead time; recommend staged activation over 4 weeks (8 → 16 → 32) with canary at 8 for 2 weeks- Burst strategy: configured hot-standby pod for 2-hour daily peak windows (subject to reserved capacity policy)

Option C — Growth / High-Availability- Minimum reserved: 88–96 GPUs (12 x 8-GPU nodes)- Topology: multi-rack distributed cluster with regional redundancy if needed- Expected steady throughput: 1,200+ reqs/minute; p50 ~100–150ms with aggressive batching and KV caching- Use case: enterprise scale with SLA-backed latency and high burst headroom- Activation: 8–10 week runway; staged activation with on-call prewarming and automated warm-start scripts- Burst strategy: guaranteed headroom and priority routing, included in enterprise SLA

Operational notes (all options):
- Model assumptions: 30B quantized to fp16/4-bit (we benchmarked on L40-class hardware). Rerank/7B tasks can be colocated on same nodes for light usage.
- Warm-start: recommend daily prewarm jobs during activation window; persistent KV cache yields up to ~40% p95 reduction for repeat prefixes.
- Autoscaling: limited by reservation; we use a policy that allows intra-pool scaling and graceful fallback to hosted when reserved exhausted (configurable).
- Billing: monthly reserved fee + token/usage overage model for bursts. Exact numbers in attached pricing sheet.

Next steps: Ben to draft a one-pager with prices and a DocuSign packet; Jordan to send to Evan and Contracts after Marissa's sign-off.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
